statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk is low at 12% while stress is elevated at 60% after a four-session Nasdaq-100 drawdown driven by long-end Treasury yields and an energy-price shock.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Concentrated conditional risk is assessed around the 13:30 UTC cash open with the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, and most of all around the monthly options-expiration close, which is published as the narrow danger window at 19:00-20:00 UTC. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 grinds to a fourth lower close on long-end yield stress, but intraday retracements and a 16 VIX keep mean reversion intact
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,213.17 on 20 August, down 0.72% and roughly 2.8% on the week, its fourth consecutive lower close. The decline has been a grind rather than a rout: the 20 August session opened at 29,295.15, traded a 260-point range between 29,378.80 and 29,118.33, and closed about 95 points off the low, so retracements have remained available on every day of the drawdown. The driver is the long end of the Treasury curve. The 30-year yield reached its highest level in nearly two decades on 18 August and finished 20 August above 5.25%, while the 10-year rose about four basis points to roughly 4.69% after the relief from the Treasury's buyback intervention proved short-lived. July FOMC minutes released 19 August were hawkish, with three voting members dissenting in favour of a quarter-point increase. A second channel is energy: crude rose roughly 3% on 20 August, taking Brent above $93 and WTI above $86, after US statements on economic pressure against Iran. Walmart fell more than 9% on slowing comparable sales, adding a consumer-demand signal. Against that, the evidence for a mean-reversion failure is thin. The VIX closed at 16.01, low in absolute terms despite a 7.5% rise. Latest-session internals are split rather than aligned, with semiconductors firm and seven of eight tracked megacaps lower. Overnight, NQ futures hold a narrow range of roughly 0.31% with a modest positive drift, VIX futures are slightly lower and crude has given back a fraction of Thursday's gain. That combination supports low tail risk with elevated stress. Today's scheduled catalyst is the medium-impact S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC, shortly after the cash open; the more relevant structural feature is the monthly options expiration settling into the 20:00 UTC close, which is the one interval where hedging flow could plausibly suppress retracements.

The most recent Claude snapshot in this repository is dated 2026-08-17T14:33:11Z, so the entire lookback window falls inside a provider publication gap and every slot is marked unavailable with null assessment fields. Past opinions are not reconstructed from later information. For context established from independent research rather than from provider history, the Nasdaq-100 fell on each of 17, 18, 19 and 20 August, with the largest single-day decline of 1.68% on 18 August.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour horizon runs from the current Asian hours through a full European and US session and ends inside the weekend closure. Asian and early European hours are scored at low tail risk on contained overnight ranges. Conditional risk rises through the European flash PMI block and then to watch level for the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, where two-way repricing is the base case. The single highest forecast tail score falls on the 19:00-20:00 UTC hour, when the monthly options expiration settles into the US cash close and hedging flow could plausibly suppress retracements; that hour is published as the danger window. CME equity index futures close for the week at 21:00 UTC, so the final three forecast hours carry no tradable price path and tail risk falls to its floor, leaving weekend gap exposure as the residual. Beyond this horizon, the concentrated cluster is 26 August, when the second estimate of Q2 GDP and the July Core PCE price index are both released at 12:30 UTC.
